You are working with a pinned snapshot of Osprey/FID-A, a magnetic resonance
spectroscopy processing pipeline. A collaborator is processing edited MRS data
with multiple subspectra. In a reduced synthetic reproduction, one acquisition
condition has a 180 degree polarity relationship to the others, and the current
pipeline produces an inconsistent aligned/combined result.

Run python reproduce.py and repair the source under source/
so that edited subspectra are handled consistently before alignment and
combination. The repair should be general across edited MRS datasets and
ordinary load/process workflows.

# Osprey/FID-A Edited MRS Processing Notes

These notes are a compact offline oracle for the task. They summarize public
Osprey/FID-A workflow concepts and standard edited magnetic resonance
spectroscopy processing semantics.

## Osprey and FID-A

Osprey is an all-in-one software suite for processing and quantitative analysis
of in-vivo magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) data. Its workflow separates
loading, preprocessing, fitting, quantification, and reporting. FID-A is an
open-source MATLAB toolbox used for MRS simulation and processing. Osprey
bundles and builds on FID-A-style data structures and processing functions.

An MRS dataset is often represented in two linked forms:

- `fids`: complex time-domain free induction decay samples;
- `specs`: frequency-domain spectra obtained by Fourier transform.

The structure also carries axes and dimension metadata such as time, averages,
and subspectra. Operations that scale or phase a spectrum generally need to keep
the time-domain and frequency-domain representations consistent.

## Edited MRS Subspectra

Edited MRS methods such as MEGA editing, HERMES, and HERCULES acquire multiple
related subspectra. Each subspectrum corresponds to a different editing
condition. The final analysis often combines or subtracts these conditions so
that an edited metabolite signal can be isolated from stronger overlapping
background resonances.

This means the subspectra are not independent unrelated experiments. They are
paired or grouped observations of the same sample under different acquisition
conditions. Common resonances should remain comparable across subspectra before
alignment and combination.

## Phase and Polarity

A 180 degree phase shift changes the sign of a real-valued resonance peak. In a
simple picture, a positive peak at a reference resonance becomes a negative peak
with the same shape. If one subspectrum is averaged or aligned against an
inverted copy of the same common signal, the common component can cancel or
distort.

For edited MRS processing, this is not a cosmetic plotting issue. Frequency and
phase alignment procedures assume that common reference features have compatible
polarity. Difference spectra also assume that the signals being subtracted have
the intended sign relationship. If a common reference peak is accidentally
opposite signed before alignment, the algorithm can estimate the wrong
correction or produce a difference spectrum with suppressed signal.

Stable singlet-like resonances, commonly including creatine-like signal around
3 ppm in proton MRS examples, are frequently used as reference features for
quality checks, frequency/phase correction, or polarity assessment.

## Load Stage and Process Stage

An MRS processing pipeline can manipulate phase or polarity at more than one
stage. A loader may split raw acquisition rows into subspectra and may also undo
phase cycling. A later processing stage may classify subspectra, estimate
polarity, align them, and combine or subtract them.

These stages are coupled. If the loader removes or changes polarity information
too early, the processing stage may no longer be able to determine how the
subspectra should be aligned. Conversely, if the process stage assumes all
subspectra are already polarity-consistent when they are not, alignment and
combination can be scientifically invalid.

The correct behavior is not "always flip everything". Some workflows
intentionally preserve original acquisition polarity for a specific analysis.
The pipeline must distinguish that case from the ordinary edited-MRS workflow
where common reference components should be polarity-consistent before alignment
and combination.

## Reasoning Target

For this task, the public synthetic fixture models a small edited-MRS dataset
with a common reference peak and one polarity-inverted acquisition condition.
The expected scientific behavior is:

1. identify that the common reference component is polarity-inconsistent across
   subspectra;
2. make the subspectra comparable before alignment and combination in the
   normal corrected workflow;
3. preserve a distinct path for workflows that intentionally keep the original
   acquisition polarity;
4. keep loader-stage handling and process-stage handling consistent.

The source repair should implement the workflow semantics generally. It should
not special-case this fixture.
No binary assets are required for this reduced task. The public oracle material
is in `paper.md`.

    26	% DEPENDENCIES:
    27	% This function requires the dcm2nii toolbox (Xiangrui Li) to be on the
    28	% MATLAB path

    30	%

    36	
    37	function out = io_loadspec_niimrs(filename,undoPhaseCycle)
    38	
    39	if nargin < 2

    42	
    43	% Read in the data using the dicm2nii toolbox
    44	% (https://github.com/xiangruili/dicm2nii)
    45	try
    46	    nii = nii_tool('load', filename);

    52	                ' dcm2nii toolbox (https://github.com/xiangruili/dicm2nii)', ...
    53	                ' and added it to your MATLAB path.']);

    58	
    59	% Extract the header and header extensions
    60	hdr = nii.hdr;

    71	% Specify dimensions
    72	% In NIfTI MRS, the three spatial dimensions and the time dimension occupy
    73	% fixed indices in the (maximum) 7-D array

    75	dims.y = 2;
    76	dims.z = 3;
    77	dims.t = 4;
    78	
    79	% There are some pre-defined dimension names according to the FID-A
    80	% convention. These dimensions may or may not be stored in the NIfTI MRS
    81	% header, so we'll initialize them as 0.
    82	dims.coils = 0;
    83	dims.averages = 0;
    84	dims.subSpecs = 0;
    85	dims.extras = 0;

    87	% The NIfTI MRS standard reserves the remaining 3 dimensions, which are
    88	% then explicitly specified in the JSON header extension fields dim_5,
    89	% dim_6 and dim_7.
    90	if isfield(hdr_ext, 'dim_5')

    92	
    93	    % This field may come in as a cell or a string.
    94	    if iscell(hdr_ext.dim_5)

    97	        dim_5 = hdr_ext.dim_5;
    98	    end
    99	    switch dim_5
   100	        case 'DIM_COIL'

   102	        case 'DIM_DYN'
   103	            dims.averages   = dim_number;
   104	        case 'DIM_INDIRECT_0'
   105	            dims.extras     = dim_number;
   106	        case 'DIM_INDIRECT_1'
   107	            dims.extras     = dim_number;
   108	        case 'DIM_INDIRECT_2'
   109	            dims.extras     = dim_number;
   110	        case 'DIM_PHASE_CYCLE'
   111	            dims.extras     = dim_number;
   112	        case 'DIM_EDIT'
   113	            dims.subSpecs   = dim_number;
   114	        case 'DIM_MEAS'
   115	            dims.extras     = dim_number;
   116	        case 'DIM_USER_0'
   117	            dims.extras     = dim_number;
   118	        case 'DIM_USER_1'
   119	            dims.extras     = dim_number;
   120	        case 'DIM_USER_2'
   270	        switch MRSCont.datatype
   271	            case 'NIfTI-MRS'
   272	                [MRSCont] = osp_LoadNII(MRSCont);
   273	            otherwise
   274	                msg = 'Data type not supported. Please contact the Osprey team (gabamrs@gmail.com).';
   275	                fprintf(msg);
   276	                error(msg);
   277	        end
   278	    otherwise
   279	        msg = 'Vendor not supported. Please contact the Osprey team (gabamrs@gmail.com).';

   281	        error(msg);
   282	end
   283	
   284	% Perform coil combination (SENSE-based reconstruction if PRIAM flag set)
   285	if ~MRSCont.flags.isPRIAM && ~MRSCont.flags.isMRSI

   291	        end
   292	    end
   293	elseif MRSCont.flags.isPRIAM
   294	    [MRSCont] = osp_senseRecon(MRSCont);
   295	elseif MRSCont.flags.isMRSI && ~strcmp(MRSCont.datatype,'DATA')

   297	end
   298	
   299	if MRSCont.flags.isUnEdited
   300	    for kk = 1:MRSCont.nDatasets(1)
   301	        raw                         = MRSCont.raw{kk};                                          % Get the kk-th dataset
   302	
   303	        %%% MERGE MULTIPLE DIMENSIONS %%%
   304	        % If the dimensionality of the dataset isn't just along the
   305	        % 'averages' dimension, we re-sort the other dimensions into the
   306	        % 'averages' dimension here. This can be the case when some
   307	        % sequences divide the entire acquisition into dynamics, which are
   308	        % then again divided into transients.
   309	        % This does NOT apply to SPECIAL-localized data - here, the
   310	        % different dimensions have an explicit meaning and need to be
   311	        % preserved.
   312	        % This is also NOT the case for data acquired with the series
   313	        % function!
   314	        if ~MRSCont.flags.isSPECIAL && ~MRSCont.flags.isSERIES
   315	            if raw.dims.extras ~= 0

   317	                temp = struct;
   318	                % Extract extras and add to the temporary struct
   319	                for pp = 1:raw.sz(raw.dims.extras)
   320	                    extrasToAdd = op_takeextras(raw, pp);
   321	                    temp = op_concatAverages(temp, extrasToAdd);
   322	                end
   323	                % Save back to MRSCont
   324	                raw = temp;
   325	                MRSCont.raw{kk} = raw;
   326	            elseif raw.dims.subSpecs ~= 0
   327	                % Generate empty struct

   335	                raw = temp;
   245	%%          %%% 3. FREQUENCY/PHASE CORRECTION AND AVERAGING %%%

   257	                        case 'RobSpecReg'

   259	                        case 'RestrSpecReg'

   261	                                [raw, fs, phs, weights, driftPre, driftPost]     = op_SpecRegFreqRestrict(raw, seq, 0,refShift_ind_ini,0,MRSCont.opts.SpecRegRange(1),MRSCont.opts.SpecRegRange(2)); % Align and average
   262	                            else
   263	                                [raw, fs, phs, weights, driftPre, driftPost]     = op_SpecRegFreqRestrict(raw, seq, 0,refShift_ind_ini,0,MRSCont.opts.fit.range(1),MRSCont.opts.fit.range(2)); % Align and average
   264	                            end
   265	                        case 'none'
   266	                            [raw, fs, phs, weights, driftPre, driftPost]     = op_SpecRegFreqRestrict(raw, seq, 0,refShift_ind_ini,1); % Align and average
   267	                    end
   268	                else
   269	                    switch MRSCont.opts.SpecReg %Pick spectral registration method (default is Robust Spectral Registration)
   270	                        case 'none'
   271	                            [raw, fs, phs, weights, driftPre, driftPost]     = op_SpecRegFreqRestrict(raw, seq, 0,refShift_ind_ini,1); % Align and average
   272	                        otherwise
   273	                            [raw, fs, phs, weights, driftPre, driftPost]   = op_SpecRegFreqRestrict(raw, seq, 0,refShift_ind_ini,0,0.5,4.2);
   274	                    end
   275	                end
   276	
   277	                raw.specReg{1}.fs              = fs; % save align parameters
   278	                raw.specReg{1}.phs             = phs; % save align parameters
   279	                if raw.flags.isUnEdited
   280	                    raw.specReg{1}.weights         = weights; % save align parameters);
   281	                    raw.specReg{1}.weights{1}         = raw.specReg{1}.weights{1}'/max(raw.specReg{1}.weights{1}(1,:));
   282	                end
   283	                if raw.flags.isMEGA
   284	                    raw.specReg{1}.weights         = weights; % save align parameters);
   285	                    raw.specReg{1}.weights{1} = raw.specReg{1}.weights{1}'/(max(raw.specReg{1}.weights{1}(1,:)));
   286	                    raw.specReg{1}.weights{2} = raw.specReg{1}.weights{2}'/(max(raw.specReg{1}.weights{2}(1,:)));
   287	                end
   288	                if raw.flags.isHERMES || raw.flags.isHERCULES
   289	                    raw.specReg{1}.weights         = weights; % save align parameters);
   290	                    raw.specReg{1}.weights{1} = raw.specReg{1}.weights{1}'/(max(raw.specReg{1}.weights{1}(1,:)));
   291	                    raw.specReg{1}.weights{2} = raw.specReg{1}.weights{2}'/(max(raw.specReg{1}.weights{2}(1,:)));
   292	                    raw.specReg{1}.weights{3} = raw.specReg{1}.weights{3}'/(max(raw.specReg{1}.weights{3}(1,:)));
   293	                    raw.specReg{1}.weights{4} = raw.specReg{1}.weights{4}'/(max(raw.specReg{1}.weights{4}(1,:)));
   294	                end
   295	
   296	            else
   297	                % If there is still an average dimension, squeeze
   298	                if raw.dims.averages > 0
   299	                    raw.fids = squeeze(sum(raw.fids, raw.dims.averages));
   300	                    raw.specs=fftshift(fft(raw.fids,[],raw.dims.t),raw.dims.t);
   301	                    if raw.dims.t>raw.dims.averages
   302	                        raw.dims.t=raw.dims.t-1;

   304	                        raw.dims.t=raw.dims.t;
   305	                    end

   309	                        raw.dims.coils=raw.dims.coils;
   310	                    end
   311	                    raw.dims.averages=0;
   312	                    if raw.dims.subSpecs>raw.dims.averages

   328	                    raw.specReg{1}.phs             = 0; % save align parameters

   334	                    raw.specReg{1}.phs             = zeros(1,2); % save align parameters
   335	                    raw.specReg{1}.weights{1}         = ones(1,1); % save align parameters
   336	                    raw.specReg{1}.weights{2}         = ones(1,1); % save align parameters

   338	                    driftPre{2} = 0;

   342	                    raw.specReg{1}.phs             = zeros(1,4); % save align parameters
   343	                    raw.specReg{1}.weights{1}         = ones(1,1); % save align parameters
   344	                    raw.specReg{1}.weights{2}         = ones(1,1); % save align parameters
   345	                    raw.specReg{1}.weights{3}         = ones(1,1); % save align parameters
   346	                    raw.specReg{1}.weights{4}         = ones(1,1); % save align parameters
   347	                    driftPre{1} = 0;
   348	                    driftPre{2} = 0;
   349	                    driftPre{3} = 0;
   350	                    driftPre{4} = 0;
   351	                end
   352	                driftPost = driftPre;
   353	            end
   354	
   355	%%          %%% 4. GET REFERENCE DATA / EDDY CURRENT CORRECTION %%%
   356	            % If there are reference scans, load them here to allow eddy-current

   361	                        if MRSCont.opts.ECC.mm(mm_ref_ll,kk)

   387	            
   388	%%          %%% 5. DETERMINE POLARITY OF SPECTRUM (EG FOR MOIST WATER SUPP) %%%
   389	            % Automate determination whether the Cr peak has positive polarity.
   390	            % For water suppression methods like MOIST, the residual water may
   391	            % actually have negative polarity, but end up positive in the data, so
   392	            % that the spectrum needs to be flipped.
   393	            if ~isfield(MRSCont.opts.SubSpecAlignment, 'polResidCr')

   398	                    % of the respective peak is positive; if the absolute of the maximum
   399	                    % minus the absolute of the minimum is negative, the polarity is negative.
   400	                    polResidCr = abs(max(real(raw_Cr.specs))) - abs(min(real(raw_Cr.specs)));

   418	                polResidCr39(polResidCr39>0) = 1;

   425	            end

   458	                    MRSCont.QM.drift.pre.B{kk} = driftPre{2};
   459	                    MRSCont.QM.drift.post.A{kk} = driftPost{1};
   460	                    MRSCont.QM.drift.post.B{kk} = driftPost{1};

   494	                raw.specReg{1}.weights = raw.specReg{1}.weights(:,commuteOrder);
   495	                % Save drift information back to container
   496	                MRSCont.QM.drift.pre.A{kk} = driftPre{1};
   497	                MRSCont.QM.drift.pre.B{kk} = driftPre{2};
   498	                MRSCont.QM.drift.pre.C{kk} = driftPre{3};
   499	                MRSCont.QM.drift.pre.D{kk} = driftPre{4};
   500	                MRSCont.QM.drift.post.A{kk} = driftPost{1};
   501	                MRSCont.QM.drift.post.B{kk} = driftPost{2};
   502	                MRSCont.QM.drift.post.C{kk} = driftPost{3};
   503	                MRSCont.QM.drift.post.D{kk} = driftPost{4};
   504	                % Generate the drift plot for the entire experiment in
   505	                % the correct order
   506	                driftPre = [MRSCont.QM.drift.pre.A{kk}, MRSCont.QM.drift.pre.B{kk}, MRSCont.QM.drift.pre.C{kk}, MRSCont.QM.drift.pre.D{kk}]';
   507	                try
   508	                    driftPre = reshape(driftPre, [raw.averages, 1]);
   509	                catch
   510	                    driftPre = reshape(driftPre, [raw.rawAverages, 1]);
   511	                end
   512	                MRSCont.QM.drift.pre.diff1{kk}  = driftPre;
   513	                MRSCont.QM.drift.pre.diff2{kk}  = driftPre;
   514	                if exist('target3', 'var') % For HERMES 4 acqusitions
   515	                    MRSCont.QM.drift.pre.diff3{kk}  = driftPre;

"},{"type":"input_text","text":"     1	% philipsLoad.m
     2	% Georg Oeltzschner, Johns Hopkins University 2018.
     3	%
     4	% USAGE:
     5	% [data, header] = philipsLoad(filename);
     6	% 
     7	% DESCRIPTION:
     8	% Reads in philips MRS data (.spar and .sdat files) using code adapted from 
     9	% PhilipsRead.m, provided as part of the Gannet software package by Richard 
    10	% Edden (gabamrs.com).
    11	% 
    12	% INPUTS:
    13	% filename   = filename of Philips .sdat file to be loaded.
    14	%
    15	% OUTPUTS:
    16	% data       = FID array.
    17	% header     = Structure containing header information from SPAR file.
    18	
    19	function [data, header] = philipsLoad(filename)
    20	
    21	% Get the .spar filename
    22	sparname = [filename(1:(end-4)) 'spar'];
    23	% Populate the header information from the SPAR file
    24	% Look for regular expression separated by a colon
    25	fid_spar = fopen(sparname);
    26	if fid_spar == -1
    27	    sparname = [filename(1:(end-4)) 'SPAR']; %This seems to be a problem for some Linux based systems
    28	    fid_spar = fopen(sparname);
    29	end
    30	while ~feof(fid_spar)
    31	    tline = fgets(fid_spar); % get first line
    32	    [tokens,matches] = regexp(tline,'([\w\[\].]*)\s*:\s*([-\w\s.\"\\:\.]*)','tokens','match');
    33	        % When a matching string is found, parse the results into a struct
    34	        if length(tokens) == 1
    35	            fieldname = regexprep(tokens{1}{1}, '\[|\]',''); % delete invalid characters
    36	            
    37	            % Convert numbers to doubles, leave strings & empty lines alone
    38	            if ~isnan(str2double(tokens{1}{2}))
    39	                value = str2double(tokens{1}{2});
    40	            else
    41	                value = tokens{1}{2};
    42	            end
    43	
    44	            header.(fieldname) = value;
    45	
    46	        end
    47	end
    48	fclose(fid_spar);
    49	
    50	% Now open the SDAT file and read in the data
    51	fid_sdat    = fopen(filename,'r','ieee-le');
    52	sdat_length = length(fread(fid_sdat));
    53	fclose(fid_sdat);
    54	fid_sdat    = fopen(filename,'r','ieee-le');
    55	data        = freadVAXG(fid_sdat,sdat_length,'float32');
    56	fclose(fid_sdat);
    57	% Reshape and save
    58	if isfield(header, 'nr_of_slices_for_multislice') && header.nr_of_slices_for_multislice > 1
    59	    data        = reshape(data, [2 header.samples header.rows header.nr_of_slices_for_multislice]);
    60	    data        = squeeze(data(1,:,:,:)+1i*data(2,:,:,:));
    61	else
    62	    data        = reshape(data, [2 header.samples header.rows]);    
    63	    data        = squeeze(data(1,:,:)+1i*data(2,:,:));
    64	end
    65	end

     2	function [out] = op_combine_water_subspecs(in,average)
     3	% Some formats end up having subspectra in their reference scans
     4	% (e.g. Philips), as well as empty lines. Intercept these cases
     5	% here.
     6	if nargin < 2
     7	    average = 1;
     8	end
     9	    out = in;
    10	    if out.subspecs == 2
    11	        raw_A               = op_takesubspec(out,1);
    12	        [raw_A]             = op_rmempty(raw_A);            % Remove empty lines
    13	        raw_B               = op_takesubspec(out,2);
    14	        [raw_B]             = op_rmempty(raw_B);            % Remove empty lines
    15	        out                 = op_concatAverages(raw_A,raw_B);
    16	    end
    17	
    18	    if out.subspecs == 4
    19	        raw_A               = op_takesubspec(out,1);
    20	        [raw_A]             = op_rmempty(raw_A);            % Remove empty lines
    21	        raw_B               = op_takesubspec(out,2);
    22	        [raw_B]             = op_rmempty(raw_B);            % Remove empty lines
    23	        raw_C               = op_takesubspec(out,3);
    24	        [raw_C]             = op_rmempty(raw_C);            % Remove empty lines
    25	        raw_D               = op_takesubspec(out,4);
    26	        [raw_D]             = op_rmempty(raw_D);            % Remove empty lines
    27	        out                 = op_concatAverages(op_concatAverages(raw_A,raw_B),op_concatAverages(raw_C,raw_D));
    28	    end
    29	    if out.subspecs == 1
    30	        [out]             = op_rmempty(out);            % Remove empty lines
    31	    end
    32	    if average
    33	        % Align and verage the refernce data
    34	        if out.averages > 1 && ~out.flags.averaged
    35	            [out]             = op_rmempty(out);
    36	            [out,~,~]               = op_alignAverages(out, 1, 'n');
    37	            out                     = op_averaging(out);            % Average
    38	        else
    39	            out.flags.averaged  = 1;
    40	            out.dims.averages   = 0;
    41	        end
    42	    end
    43	    out.names = {'A'};
    44	end

     4	% USAGE:

     7	% DESCRIPTION:
     8	% Extract the subspectra with indices corresponding to the 'index' input

    10	% 
    11	% INPUTS:
    12	% in     = input data in matlab structure format.
    13	% index  = vector indicating the indices of the subspectra you would like

    15	%
    16	% OUTPUTS:
    17	% out    = Output dataset consisting of subspectra indices extracted from 
    18	%          the input.
    19	
    20	function out=op_takesubspec(in,index);
    21	
    22	if ~isnumeric(index)
    23	    index = find(strcmp(in.names,index));
    24	    if isempty(index)
    25	        index = 1;
    26	    end
    27	end
    28	
    29	if in.flags.subtracted && ~strcmp(in.seq, 'SPECIAL')
    30	    error('ERROR:  Subspectra have already been combined!  Aborting!');
    31	end
    32	% in.fids = squeeze(in.fids);
    33	if in.dims.subSpecs==0
    34	    %Can't take subspec because there are none:
    35	    if index > 1
    36	        error('ERROR:  There are no subspectra in this dataset!  Aborting!');
    37	    else
    38	        fids = in.fids;
    39	    end
    40	elseif in.dims.subSpecs==1
    41	    %SHOULD NEVER HAPPEN (Time dimension should always be dim=1)
    42	    error('ERROR:  dims.subSpecs==1.  This should never happen!  Aborting!');
    43	elseif in.dims.subSpecs==2
    44	    fids=in.fids(:,index,:,:,:);
    45	elseif in.dims.subSpecs==3;
    46	    fids=in.fids(:,:,index,:,:,:);
    47	elseif in.dims.subSpecs==4;
    48	    fids=in.fids(:,:,:,index,:,:,:);
    49	elseif in.dims.subSpecs==5
    50	    fids=in.fids(:,:,:,:,index,:,:,:);
    51	end
    52	
    53	%re-calculate Specs using fft
    54	specs=fftshift(fft(fids,[],in.dims.t),in.dims.t);
    55	
    56	%change the dims variables
    57	if in.dims.t>in.dims.subSpecs && in.dims.subSpecs ~=0
    58	    dims.t=in.dims.t-1;
    59	else
    60	    dims.t=in.dims.t;
    61	end
    62	if in.dims.coils>in.dims.subSpecs && in.dims.subSpecs ~=0
    63	    dims.coils=in.dims.coils-1;
    64	else
    65	    dims.coils=in.dims.coils;
    66	end
    67	if in.dims.averages>in.dims.subSpecs && in.dims.subSpecs ~=0
    68	    dims.averages=in.dims.averages-1;
    69	else
    70	    dims.averages=in.dims.averages;
    71	end
    72	if in.dims.extras>in.dims.subSpecs && in.dims.subSpecs ~=0
    73	    dims.extras=in.dims.extras-1;
    74	else
    75	    dims.extras=in.dims.extras;
    76	end
    77	dims.subSpecs=0;
    78	
    79	%re-calculate the sz variable
    80	sz=size(fids);
    81	
    82	
    83	%FILLING IN DATA STRUCTURE
    84	out=in;
    85	out.fids=fids;
    86	out.specs=specs;
    87	out.sz=sz;
    88	out.dims=dims;

    91	        out.averages = out.sz(out.dims.averages);
    92	    catch
    93	        out.averages = out.sz(2);
    94	    end
    95	end

    97	if isfield(out, 'names')
    98	    out.names = out.names(index);
    99	end
